newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas mixed late, Sept holds new range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas mixed late, Sept holds new range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared early gains and turned mixed late Monday in sluggish trade, but reports of firm physical prices seemed to limit September's downside for now, sources said.
By 1435 EDT, September slipped 0.7 cent to $2.425 per million British thermal units, while October was 2.9 cents lower at $2.435. Other months were narrowly mixed.

"The weather is moderate just about everywhere but cash is up. It's got to be storage," said one Texas-based trader, noting still-hot Texas temperatures but cooler trends in California and across northern tier states.
Despite the lack of weather support, traders agreed lagging inventories, still almost 10 percent below the three-year average, have put a floor under the market.

Technical traders still pegged September support at Friday's low of $2.395, then at $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely in the $2.25-2.27 area. Resistance was seen at $2.55 and then at the contract high and double top at $2.605. Further selling was likely in the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices firmed three cents into the low-to-mid $2.50s. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-to-mid $2.40s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher in the mid-to-high $2.70s.
NYMEX said 26,678 contracts traded at 1400 EDT.
On KCBT, September eased 1.2 cents to $2.35, while deferreds were steady to 2.2 cents lower. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 7.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
